title: The Lemon Slice
teaser: Sir Clive collapsed at 9:42. The poison takes half an hour to work. Something he swallowed after nine o'clock was not what it seemed.

booklet.briefing:
Sir Clive Marbury, owner of Marbury Shipping, hosted five guests for dinner on Friday. At 9:42 pm he gasped, clutched his chest and collapsed. The quick-thinking butler called an ambulance, and Sir Clive survived, but only just.

The hospital found aconite in his blood, a plant poison. Someone at the table tried to kill him.

Everyone shared the same food from the same dishes, and the same wine from the same decanter. Mr. Foxy wants to know exactly what Sir Clive swallowed, and exactly when.
rules: The poison was swallowed at the dinner table.
The five suspects were the only other people at the table. The butler served but never touched Sir Clive's glasses after 8:55 (confirmed by the photos).

suspects.name: Lady Hester Marbury
suspects.description: Sat at the far end of the table, facing her husband.
suspects.motive: Their marriage has been cold for years.
suspects.statement: I didn't move from my seat all evening. The table is far too long to reach Clive from my end.

suspects.name: Gordon Pruitt
suspects.description: Sat at Sir Clive's left hand. Asked for extra lemon with his fish.
suspects.motive: Sir Clive was about to push him out of the company.
suspects.statement: I squeezed my lemon over the sole like a civilised man and left the slice on my plate.

suspects.name: Colonel Basil Marsh
suspects.description: Proposed a toast at 9:00 and walked round the table to clink glasses with Sir Clive.
suspects.motive: Lost a fortune on a Marbury ship that sank.
suspects.statement: I made my toast, clinked Clive's wine glass, and went straight back to my seat.

suspects.name: Rupert Marbury
suspects.description: Sat at Sir Clive's right hand. Inherits the company if his uncle dies.
suspects.motive: Has run up huge debts and was told on Thursday he'd been cut out of the will next month.
suspects.statement: I ate my fish, squeezed the lemon and left it on the side of the plate. I was watching the flambé like everyone else.

suspects.name: Imogen Marbury
suspects.description: Took photographs all evening for a magazine article about the house.
suspects.motive: Sir Clive refused to pay for her art school.
suspects.statement: I was taking pictures. My camera puts the time on every one. Look for yourselves.

evidence.title: Hospital toxicology
evidence.body:
Aconite poisoning.

From the amount found, symptoms begin 30 to 40 minutes after the poison is swallowed. Sir Clive collapsed at 9:42 pm.
lines: From the amount found, symptoms begin 30 to 40 minutes after the poison is swallowed. Sir Clive collapsed at 9:42 pm.

evidence.title: What Sir Clive ate and drank
evidence.body:
Everyone was served from the same dishes and the same decanter.

Time | What
8:40 | Soup, from one tureen. Everyone ate it.
8:55 | Butler fills Sir Clive's water glass from the water jug.
9:00 | Fish course (sole) served to every seat, each plate with one lemon slice. Flambé at the sideboard; all eyes on the flames, 9:00 to 9:02. Colonel's toast.
9:05 | Sir Clive's watch alarm beeps. He takes his heart pill with a long drink of water, as he does every night.
9:10 | Claret poured from the decanter for everyone. Sir Clive drinks.
9:18 | Fish plates cleared.
9:20 | Dessert. Sir Clive refuses it.

evidence.title: Police laboratory
evidence.source: Tests on everything from the table
evidence.body:
No aconite in: the soup tureen, the water jug, the claret decanter, Sir Clive's claret glass, his pill bottle.

Aconite found in: the water left in Sir Clive's water glass, and very strongly in a lemon slice found at the bottom of that glass.

Aconite found in: the water left in Sir Clive's water glass, and very strongly in a lemon slice found at the bottom of that glass.

evidence.title: Imogen's photographs
evidence.body:
8:58 pm: Sir Clive laughing. His water glass is full, with nothing in it but water.

9:01 pm: Everyone turned towards the flambé. The Colonel, standing behind Sir Clive's chair, clinks wine glasses with him, his other hand on his walking cane. Sir Clive's water glass is half hidden behind Rupert's arm. Rupert's fish plate is in front of him, out of the Colonel's reach.

9:04 pm: Sir Clive checking his watch. A pale yellow slice is floating in his water glass.

evidence.title: Sir Clive, from his hospital bed
evidence.body: “Lemon? In my water? I can't stand the stuff, everybody knows that. I took my pill without looking, I never look.”
lines: “Lemon? In my water? I can't stand the stuff, everybody knows that. I took my pill without looking, I never look.”

evidence.title: Butler's note on the fish plates
evidence.body:
Every lemon slice was still on its plate, squeezed or not, except one.

The police later searched the table, chairs and floor: no loose lemon slices anywhere.

Seat | Lemon slice on the plate?
1 (Sir Clive) | Yes, untouched
2 | No
3 | Yes, untouched
4 | Yes, squeezed
5 | Yes, squeezed
6 | Yes, squeezed (and an extra one, also squeezed)

evidence.title: Place cards
evidence.body:
Seat 1, head of the table: Sir Clive. Seat 2, his right: Rupert. Seat 3: Imogen. Seat 4, the far end: Lady Hester. Seat 5: Colonel Marsh. Seat 6, his left: Gordon Pruitt.

Only seats 2 and 6 are close enough to touch Sir Clive's glasses without standing up.

evidence.body: A tiny brown glass dropper bottle, empty, with traces of aconite tincture. Fingerprints on it: Rupert Marbury's.

questions.prompt: Between what times did Sir Clive swallow the poison?
questions.explanation: He collapsed at 9:42 and the poison works after 30 to 40 minutes. 9:42 minus 40 is 9:02, minus 30 is 9:12.
hints: The toxicology report gives you the delay. Work backwards from the collapse.
From 9:02 to 9:12. Now check the service notes for what happened then.

questions.explanation: The poison was in a lemon slice dropped into Sir Clive's water between 9:00 and 9:04. Rupert sat beside him, his slice is the only one missing, his arm hid the glass in the 9:01 photo, and the dropper bottle with his fingerprints was in the fern beside his seat.

solution.explanation: Rupert Marbury learned he was to be cut out of his uncle's will and decided to act first. He knew Sir Clive takes his heart pill at 9:05 every night with a long drink of water, without looking. When the fish arrived with its lemon slices and every head turned to the flambé, Rupert dripped aconite onto his own lemon slice under the table and dropped it into his uncle's glass. Sir Clive hates lemon and would have noticed if he'd looked. He never looks. Rupert's plate was the only one left without a slice.

chain.step: Collapse at 9:42 with a 30 to 40 minute delay: the poison was swallowed between 9:02 and 9:12.
In that window he drank water at 9:05 and claret at 9:10. Only the water glass and a lemon slice in it held poison.
The slice went in between 8:58 and 9:04, after the lemons were served at 9:00. Sir Clive hates lemon and left his own.
Only seat 2's slice is missing. Seat 2 is Rupert, right beside Sir Clive.
Rupert's arm hid the glass at 9:01, and his fingerprints are on the dropper bottle in the fern by his seat.

eliminations.name: Lady Hester Marbury
eliminations.why: At the far end of the table, out of reach, and her squeezed slice was still on her plate.

eliminations.name: Gordon Pruitt
eliminations.why: Sat close enough, but both his slices, his own and his extra, were on his plate.

eliminations.name: Colonel Basil Marsh
eliminations.why: Came close for the toast, but his own slice was still on his plate.

eliminations.name: Imogen Marbury
eliminations.why: Out of reach in seat 3, busy photographing, and her slice was untouched on her plate.
